STRAIN.Tooltip: Strain Oneself: restore your dice pool limit to its maximum. You suffer one injury.

Reasons.NOT_DAMAGED: Your dice pool limit is already at its maximum.
Reasons.MAJOR_NPC_REQUIRED: Only NPCs with the Major NPC knack can strain themselves.
Reasons.ALREADY_STRAINED: This NPC has already strained once and cannot do so again.
Reasons.PERMISSION_DENIED: You do not have permission to strain for this actor.

Dialog.Title: Strain Oneself
Dialog.Prompt: {actorName} restores their dice pool limit to its maximum.
Dialog.Price: The price: one injury, rolled right away.
Dialog.NpcOnce: A Major NPC may strain only once. If they are wounded afterwards, they are immediately killed or knocked unconscious at the GM's discretion.

Chat.Label: Strain Oneself
Chat.Summary: {actorName} strains themselves and restores their dice pool limit ({oldDicePoolValue} → {newDicePoolValue} dice).
Chat.NpcSpent: {actorName} has now used their one strain. If they are wounded again, they are out of the fight.

DAMAGE.Tooltip: Apply the damage of this attack to the target.

Reasons.ACTOR_NOT_FOUND: The target could not be found.
Reasons.PERMISSION_DENIED: You do not have permission to change this actor.
Reasons.ATTACK_MISSED: The attack missed — it deals no damage.
Reasons.DEFENDED: The target avoided the attack — it deals no damage at all (core p. 30).
Reasons.NO_CHANGE: Neither damage nor horror was entered.
Reasons.UNAVAILABLE: Damage cannot be applied right now.

Dialog.Title: Apply Damage
Dialog.HorrorHint: Optional — for spells and NPC knacks.
Dialog.WoundedWarning: {targetName} is wounded at a limit of 0 and can only strain themselves (core p. 31).
Dialog.HintsNote: Rules text only — nothing is deducted automatically. Adjust the damage by hand.
Dialog.HintsEmpty: No damage reduction found on this target.
Dialog.HorrorAtMax: {targetName} is at the maximum horror limit of {max} — further horror has no effect (core p. 36).

Chat.Label: Damage
Chat.Wounded: {targetName} is wounded — no actions until they strain themselves (core p. 31).
Chat.HorrorCapped: {requested} horror were reduced to {applied}: {targetName}'s horror limit cannot exceed their dice pool maximum.
Chat.HorrorAtMax: {targetName}'s horror limit is already at their dice pool maximum — no further horror applies.

HEALING.Tooltip: Apply the result of this healing roll to the target.

Reasons.ACTOR_NOT_FOUND: The target could not be found.
Reasons.PERMISSION_DENIED: You do not have permission to change this actor.
Reasons.INJURY_NOT_FOUND: This injury is no longer on the target.
Reasons.NOT_AN_INJURY: Only injuries can be healed — traumas never are (core p. 38).
Reasons.ROLL_FAILED: The roll failed — the horror limit stays where it is (core p. 38).
Reasons.NO_SUCCESSES: Without a success there is nothing to heal (core p. 33).
Reasons.CARD_UPDATE_FAILED: The roll card could not be extended with the healing section.
Reasons.UNAVAILABLE: Healing cannot be applied right now.

Dialog.Title: Apply Healing
Dialog.DamageHint: 1 damage per success (core p. 33). Configured item effects are already included above.
Dialog.HorrorHint: A success lowers the limit by exactly 1, no matter how many successes were rolled (core p. 38).
Dialog.InjuriesNote: Successes rolled: {successes}. Harder injuries need another roll (core p. 33-34).
Dialog.HintsNote: Recognised by their rules text only, with no configured effect — adjust the amount by hand if one of them applies.
Dialog.HintsEmpty: No medical supplies found on the healer.
Dialog.NoteEngaged: The target must be engaged or be the healer themself (core p. 29/33).
Dialog.NoteNarrative: Normal healing only happens in narrative scenes (core p. 33).
Dialog.NoteOncePerScene: One character may treat the same target only once per scene (core p. 33).

Chat.Label: Healing
Chat.RecoveryDamage: {targetName} heals {healedDamage} damage — the pool limit is back at its maximum.
Chat.RecoveryHorror: The horror limit of {targetName} drops from {oldHorror} to 0 (core p. 38).
Chat.BlockedTitle: Does not heal on its own:

Treatment.HealDamageHint: Knowledge, on oneself or an engaged target: heals 1 damage per success (core p. 33).
Treatment.HealInjuryHint: Knowledge, on oneself or an engaged target: heals an injury that needs 1-3 successes (core p. 33-34).

Horror.IntrospectionHint: Resolve, on oneself: a success lowers the horror limit by 1 (core p. 38).
Horror.CounselingHint: Presence, on a target within earshot: a success lowers its horror limit by 1 (core p. 38).

Dialog.Title: Recovery
Dialog.Note: Deliberately not tied to the world clock — the span is your call. A night's rest restores the pool limit, a week also heals light injuries and the horror limit, two weeks heal the heavier ones as well.

TRAUMA.Tooltip: Roll the trauma on table 2-2. The modifier already includes the traumas this character has.

Reasons.ACTOR_NOT_FOUND: The affected character could not be found.
Reasons.ACTOR_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED: This actor cannot suffer a trauma.
Reasons.NO_HORROR_ONES: No new ones on horror dice.

Chat.Label: Trauma
Chat.Summary: {actorName} rolled {horrorOnes} one(s) on horror dice and suffers a trauma (core p. 37).
Chat.Severity: Every further one makes it worse: modifier +{severityModifier} on the trauma roll.
Chat.Note: The roll is not made automatically — the GM decides when it happens.

AutoReport.Name: Report traumas from ones on horror dice
AutoReport.Hint: After every skill roll, ones on horror dice are reported as a trauma with a button for the trauma roll (core p. 37). Switch off to handle traumas entirely by hand.

ROLL_EFFECT_SHEET.AddSuccessesHint: Added to the counted successes after the dice are read. Grants no extra dice.
ROLL_EFFECT_SHEET.HealDamageHint: Added on top of the 1 damage per success a healing roll restores.
ROLL_EFFECT_SHEET.HealInjuryHint: An injury needs one success less to be healed — never fewer than one.
ROLL_EFFECT_SHEET.ReduceHorrorLimitHint: Added to the single step a successful Introspection or Counseling grants.
ROLL_EFFECT_SHEET.DecreaseAfterUsageHint: Every use lowers the remaining charges, even when the frequency itself is unlimited.
